newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL share index ends up on late blue-chip buying.
newsitem.headline: KL share index ends up on late blue-chip buying.

text.p: Late buying of heavyweights Tenaga Nasional and Telekom Malaysia pushed the key Kuala Lumpur share market index higher at the close, but trading volume was pathetic ahead of the Christmas holiday, dealers said.

"There was a last-minute buying in Tenaga and Telekom which took the Composite Index more than 10 points up," said an institutional dealer with a bank-backed brokerage. "That was the only excitement today."
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended 11.54 points higher at 1,209.32. The index had been hovering at just below 1,200 for most of the session.
The small-cap Second Board index was up 9.97 points at 543.62.
Tenaga rose 40 cents to 11.70 ringgit and Telekom gained 30 cents to 22.50 ringgit. Some dealers attributed the rise to year-end window dressing.

Kumpulan Fima ended down four cent at 3.34 ringgit after hitting a day's high of 3.52. The company said on Monday it had obtained approval from Malaysia's central bank to start negotiations to acquire a stake in Bank of Nova Scotia Bhd.
Market volume was 82 million shares, with gainers leading losers 391 to 169.
